+---
+assignees:

+title: Find why a scroll to the bottom in AgentThreadView can stop two rows above the last row in the hosted harness
+---
+Source: the implement step of ^sh4msc4 (the hang of the full `swift test` run).
+
+Discovery: in `ThreadFloatingControlsHostedTests`, after a press on the scroll-to-bottom pill of `AgentThreadView`, the result of the scroll to the bottom is not always the same in the off-screen harness window:
+- When an update of SwiftUI applies the scroll (the test waits for the bottom scroll target, and SwiftUI updates first), the list goes to the last row (`agent-message-conversation-m29`).
+- When a `HostedViewHarness.render()` pass of the test applies the scroll (the test calls `anchors.onScroll(.bottom)` and then `render()`, or the test resumes before the update of SwiftUI), the list stops at `agent-message-conversation-m27`, two rows above the last row. More render passes, `CATransaction.flush()`, `layoutIfNeeded()` and `display()` do not move it. The manager stays pinned (it waits for the report of the bottom rows), so the pill does not show.
+- One run gave an empty report of the rows in view after one render pass.
+- In `ConversationView` alone (`ConversationViewHostedTests.aPressOnThePillScrollsTheListToTheLastRow`), the same scroll in a render pass goes to the last row. Thus the difference is in `AgentThreadView`, possibly the `.safeAreaBar(edge: .bottom)` of the floating controls, whose height changes when the pill goes away.
+
+Do:
+- Find the cause. Tell if a user can see the same stop in the app (the list pinned, two rows above the last row, with no pill).
+- If it is a product defect, correct it with a test first.
+- Then give `ThreadFloatingControlsHostedTests.aPressOnThePillOfTheThreadRequestsTheScrollToTheBottom` a certain check that the list of the thread moves to the last row. The check must not wait for a report that only a layout pass of SwiftUI can write (no event wait that is not certain, no retry, sleep, poll, clock or time limit). #avk-8
\ No newline at end of file

 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m5ft30s0xnkf0vdyf029m76m
+  text: |-
+    ### research — root cause found (probe runs, code removed after)
+    - Probe: temporary prints in `ConversationView` (scroll geometry: offset, content size, insets) and in `ScrollAnchorManager.noteVisible`, and a temporary probe suite. Logs: scratchpad probe2.txt, probe3.txt, probe4.txt.
+    - In the thread with a composer, the bottom bar (`.safeAreaBar(edge: .bottom)` of the floating controls) gives the scroll view a bottom content inset of 114 pt (146 pt while the pill shows). The list reports only the rows in the safe area (above the bar).
+    - `ConversationView.scroll(to: .bottom)` used `position.scrollTo(id: lastRowKey, anchor: .bottom)`. After a scroll up, the lazy stack has no layout for the last rows, so SwiftUI places the target from estimated row heights. In one layout pass the content size changes many times (1471 -> 1473 -> 1613 -> 1633), and the offset goes between the true end (content + inset - viewport) and a value that puts the last row at the bottom edge of the full viewport, under the bar. The pass ends at offset 1129 for a true end of 1267 (138 pt short). The last row m29 is then 16 pt below the window and under the bar, m28 is under the bar, and the list reports m20...m27. No later pass moves it (the scroll target is used up).
+    - Same result when a non-waiting run loop pass comes between the press and the scroll. Worse result when the pin and the scroll come in one update (the order of a click in the app when the main-actor task runs before the next SwiftUI update): offset 888, last reported row m23, the manager unpins and the pill comes back.
+    - With a fixed 100 pt `.safeAreaBar` on a plain `ConversationView` (no pill), the id scroll was correct. `ConversationView` alone has no bottom inset, so its test passes.
+    - `position.scrollTo(edge: .bottom)` goes to the true end in all the same cases (offset 1265 = 1631 + 114 - 480, m29 above the bar, report m23...m29 at the bottom, pinned). The end of the content honors the content inset, and the `.sizeChanges` bottom anchor keeps the end while the rows get their real heights.
+    - Can a user see it: not confirmed in the real app (no app run, to not show a window). The harness shows the stop in every order where the scroll is applied in the same layout pass as the row layout; only the order where a SwiftUI update runs first goes to the end. Thus it is a product defect of the scroll target, not a harness artifact.

Thus the scroll is always applied in the pass of the test, and the test reads only frames after that pass. No wait for a report of the list.
